Subject: Quick follow-up on EU data residency pricing

Hi Monica — thanks again for the demo earlier. A few things I promised to surface from our side so you can feed into pricing: 

- Expected usage: 4M tokens/month starting July, ramping to ~10M tokens/month by Oct; bursty payments flows (peak windows).
- Residency requirement: mandate that token payloads and logs for EU customers stay in EU. We may still accept US routing for some non-PII analytics, but primary inference must be EU-hosted.
- Target cost: we were hoping to land somewhere near $800 / 1M tokens effective after commits/caching.
- Key constraints: latency for checkout flows should be <= 200ms (p95) for EU users; SOC2 evidence and audit trail required for our security team.

Can you confirm how much of a regional premium we should expect (US vs EU) and where caching / quantization can move the needle? Also please include any procurement steps your team needs so we can get legal looped in.

Thanks Emma — great conversation earlier. Below is a brief post-call recap + initial cost math and assumptions. I attached a pricing worksheet and a SOC2 snapshot for your security review.

Post-call recap (short):
- PayLane usage profile: ~4M TPM initial, ramping to ~10M TPM by Oct. Preferred EU residency for checkout inference.
- Latency SLO: target p95 <=200ms for EU.
- Budget aspiration: ~ $800 / 1M tokens effective after commitments & optimizations.

Initial pricing/assumptions (ballpark):
- Baseline public-hosted list (US region) for the model we demo’d: ~$950 / 1M tokens.
- EU region premium: ~ +18–25% on list prices due to higher infra and cross-region compliance (so list EU ~= $1,120–1,190 / 1M).
- Effective price levers:
  - Reserved commits (12+ month or 1-year reserve) can reduce effective unit to well below list — realistic target for 10–12M TPM commit: ~$700–$820 / 1M.
  - Caching/prefix reuse: if PayLane can cache common prompts (checkout templates), expect an effective token reduction of ~10–20% depending on hit-rate.
  - Quantized model families (8-bit/4-bit) and sharded execution for non-critical endpoints can further reduce token compute cost ~10–15%.

Example scenarios (illustrative):
- No commit, EU-hosted: ~ $1,150 / 1M tokens (list + premium).
- 12-month commit (10M TPM average) + caching (~15%): effective ~ $780 / 1M tokens.
- Dedicated capacity for latency-critical endpoints (can be combined with commit): effective unit can be negotiated lower if we take a capacity fee + token discount.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx, SOC2-snapshot.pdf

Questions for PayLane to refine numbers:
1) Are the monthly volumes sustained (flat) or highly seasonal? (you mentioned bursts during month-end)
2) What percent of traffic must be strictly EU-resident (inference + logs)? 100% or e.g., 70%?
3) Any preferred legal/billing entity or PO process we should align to upfront?

Next steps:
- If you can confirm (1–3) above, we’ll run detailed unit-econ scenarios and propose two options: (A) a 12-month commit with a blended EU effective price target near your $800 goal; (B) a staged pilot pricing for Q3 to validate latency and cache efficacy.
- Proposed follow-up call: Wed 17 Jun 10am BST (let me know if that works).

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Executive, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0192

Looping in some practical pricing levers from the deals desk. Quick thoughts: 

- Commitment thresholds: for PayLane’s stated ramp, a 12-month 10M TPM commit gets us to a meaningful TCO sweet spot. I can drive a term sheet for 10M TPM that targets ~22% off EU list, which would net an effective mid-$700s / 1M tokens when combined with expected caching.
- Regional routing: recommend routing ~70–80% of EU customers to EU region (inference + logs) to meet residency while allowing non-PII analytics to be routed to US for cost savings. We'll surface a clear per-endpoint policy in the SOW.
- Dedicated vs shared: for p95 <= 200ms, a small dedicated pool for checkout flows is recommended. We can price a dedicated capacity overlay (monthly capacity fee) and then apply a deeper per-token discount for committed volume.

I attached a draft discount term sheet for internal review (discount-term-sheet-draft.pdf).

Operational notes for Laura/Monica: if PayLane wants SOC2 artifacts, give the security team the SOC2-snapshot.pdf and we’ll prepare a short audit Q&A. If procurement needs a custom SLA or WAF rules, we can scope that as part of the SOW.
